anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Stale, incomplete, or missing optimizer statistics cause systematic cardinality misestimation and mis-costing of execution plans.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : Physical read/write capacity of the underlying storage is saturated, driving high I/O latency, deep device queues, and dominant I/O wait time in the database.
Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly : Kernel-enforced limits on file handles, shared memory, semaphores, async-I/O contexts, threads, or processes are reached, preventing the engine from allocating essential OS resources.

When all three root causes coexist, the workload is exposed to a compounded failure mode: misestimated plans choose I/O-heavy access paths and excessive spool/temporary operations; the resulting surge in physical reads, writes, and temp-file activity collides with an already bandwidth-constrained storage layer, inflating latency and queue depths. Prolonged I/O waits keep sessions and background workers alive longer, driving descriptor, thread, and AIO-context usage up to or beyond kernel limits. Once those limits are hit, new workers, parallel threads, and statistics-gathering jobs fail to spawn, producing errors about file or resource exhaustion and further preventing corrective statistics refresh.

Causal chain and mutual reinforcement: (1) Inaccurate statistics steer queries toward volume-scanning or temp-spilling plans, multiplying I/O demand. (2) Storage saturation lengthens every I/O, amplifying the cost of those suboptimal plans and delaying automatic statistics maintenance, leaving statistics even staler. (3) High latency and prolonged session lifetimes consume more OS handles, async-I/O slots, and threads; once OS limits are reached, additional I/O contexts cannot be opened, throttling the database below its configured parallelism and exacerbating throughput bottlenecks. (4) The failure of auto-stats jobs due to missing workers or file handles locks the system into a vicious cycle of ever-worsening plan quality, I/O pressure, and resource exhaustion, leading to widespread slowdowns, partial outages, or complete service interruption.

entry.official_definition: Maximum amount of time allowed to complete client authentication; if not completed in time, the server closes the connection.
entry.trigger_condition: A would-be client does not complete the authentication protocol within authentication_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The server closes the connection attempt, preventing hung clients from occupying a connection indefinitely.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
